requiredFindings.problem: Item 14.4 closes the r1 anchor split, and item 22 and item 10 then assign different rows to the same keys. Item 14.4 sends ANCHOR_SOURCE, ANCHOR_RANGE and ANCHOR_UTF8 on a provider-return view to MJ row 30 only. Item 22's producer-claim row sends those three keys, together with the Coverage keys, to MJ rows 30 and 32. Item 10 says a producer-claim key from the same view-join call takes row 30 or 32. Row 32 is J1's Coverage cause and carrier row. An anchor failure is not that condition, and H-C24 requires row 30. Item 22 also sends every refusal of item 11, every view-join key included, to the host-invariant row. Item 11 covers both the provider's own terminal Coverage and the pre-Analyze conversion. Item 14.1 classifies a clean terminal's Coverage as provider-return, and item 4 admits that Coverage at item 10's producer boundary. A provider terminal entry that fails a Coverage claim key is therefore PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION in item 14.4 and HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED in item 22. Inside item 14.4 the totality key is written without the suffix the owner appends, while the catch-all assembly row is host-invariant on both origins. An exact match on the listed token puts COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH:relation@rung:subject on the host-invariant row.

requiredFindings.fix: Make item 10, item 14.4 and item 22 name one route. On a provider-return view, ANCHOR_SOURCE, ANCHOR_RANGE and ANCHOR_UTF8 take MJ row 30 only. The Coverage producer, prerequisite and totality keys take MJ rows 30 and 32. On a host-minted view every one of those keys takes the host-invariant row. Replace item 22's single producer-claim row with those two rows, and cite NE:3529 and IE:1426-1429 on the anchor row and NE:3529, NE:3538, NE:3541 and NE:3575 on the Coverage row. Change item 22's host-minted row from "items 11, 16, 18" to "item 11's pre-Analyze conversion, item 16 and item 18". Leave item 4's provider-authored terminal Coverage on the provider-return rows. Retitle item 11 so only the pre-Analyze conversion is called host-minted. In item 14.4, write the owner suffixes the way the prerequisite keys already use a star: COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH:*, SUBJECT_SCOPE_PARTITION_OVERLAP:* and SUBJECT_SCOPE_RUNG_NOT_IN_RELATION_LADDER:*. State that a star or a :<…> marker matches the owner's full key, so those prefixed keys do not fall through to the assembly catch-all.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: F3's (relation, resolution) pair plus F7 does make FACT_SCOPE_JOIN unreachable for a provider fact that passed both, so routing that key as a host invariant is sound. The reason is DLV:972-975: crossUniverseRelations is exactly imports, calls and references, which are the admitted-target relations, and key construction emits one key per activated semantic universe for those relations and one same-universe key otherwise. F7's same-only clause forces every other relation onto the child universe, which is that intra-universe key. F7 still cites NE:3162-3164, which is the 64-hex universe spelling. On the next touch, cite DLV:972-975 beside F7.
